text.p: Australian multi-media group PMP Communications Ltd announced on Thursday that it had started restructuring its divisions because of soft retail sales and that it now expected earnings before tax and abnormals for the year to June 30 to be down about 15-20 percent on 1995/96.
The company, which is about 45 percent owned by The News Corp Ltd, said the tight trading conditions referred to by PMP chairman Ken Cowley in February this year had continued.

"As a consequence of these continuing trading conditions in Australia, and a decline in New Zealand's previously buoyant economy, PMP has reviewed and restructured its operations in divisions which are most susceptible to consumer demand," it said.
"These include the catalogue printing business, book manufacturing, the pre-press business, and compact disc manufacturing."

The company also said some uneconomic printing presses have been closed while PMP has reviewed its printing operations in Batam Island, Indonesia, and would write down the carrying value to a recoverable amount in the current year.

"Results from the publishing division continue to be affected by diminished magazine advertising volumes, although the company is well placed for the future with the successful launch of For Me (in Australia) and B (in the UK)."
PMP achieved a 1995/96 (July June) net profit of A$58.04 million from A$64.44 million a year earlier while operating profit rose slightly to A$90.38 million from A$89.55 million.
